summary: Found multiple soundness gaps: arbitrary and gate-bypassing transitions, a race that reverses gated statuses, unenforced claim ownership, incomplete spec_check failure handling, hardened-review bypass, and unsafe default-branch verification.

findings.claim: The declared state machine is not enforced; advance permits any valid status to transition directly to any other valid status.
findings.evidence: tracker_advance validates only that the destination appears in VALID_STATUSES, then unconditionally writes it. For example, `advance <queued-file> done` or `advance <built-file> queued` succeeds despite neither being a declared edge.

findings.claim: claim can bypass all refusal gates by choosing gated workflow destinations directly.
findings.evidence: tracker_claim accepts arbitrary valid FROM and TO values and directly executes `_tracker_set_field "$target" status "$to"`. Thus `claim queued specd ...` skips spec_check and irreversibility checks, while `claim reviewing pr-open ...` skips hardened-report verification, because those checks exist only in tracker_advance.

findings.claim: A concurrent shelve or supersede can be silently undone by advance despite the promised gated-status protection.
findings.evidence: tracker_advance reads and checks `cur` before acquiring tracker_lock. After acquiring the lock it rereads `prev` but does not reapply the gated-status check before writing. An advance that reads a normal status, waits while another invocation shelves the file, then acquires the lock will overwrite `shelved`.

findings.claim: Claim ownership and the stated single-writer rule are not enforced.
findings.evidence: A claim records claimed_by, but mutating operations do not authenticate or compare an actor against it; tracker_advance does not even accept an actor argument. Any invocation can advance, shelve, supersede, restore, or rewire a claimed file.
findings.searched: tracker_claim, tracker_advance, tracker_shelve, tracker_restore, tracker_supersede, tracker_dep_drop, and tracker_dep_replace in scripts/lib/tracker.sh

findings.claim: The spec_check refusal gate is fail-open for failures other than exit 2 and when the checker is unavailable.
findings.evidence: The checker runs only when `-x`, and only `_sc -eq 2` causes refusal. Any other nonzero result proceeds to specd, while a missing or non-executable checker is silently skipped, contrary to blocking a spec that fails spec_check.

findings.claim: A hardened spec can reach pr-open without a hardened report when profile resolution itself fails.
findings.evidence: The gate captures `_pf="$(tracker_profile "$1" 2>/dev/null || true)"` and checks the report only when `_pf == hardened`. If the hardened payload is absent, tracker_profile returns 6 and emits no stdout, so `_pf` is empty and advance continues to pr-open without checking a report.

findings.claim: Superseded citations can be incorrectly verified against a feature branch rather than the default branch.
findings.evidence: When origin/HEAD is unavailable, `_tracker_supersede_lands` falls back to the currently checked-out HEAD. In a repository checked out on a feature branch, a commit unique to that branch passes `merge-base --is-ancestor`, unblocking dependents even though it is not on the default branch.

key_decisions: Treated the documented transition graph and refusal gates as mandatory invariants, including for generic claim/advance entry points.
caveats: Blind one-pass static review; external scripts and callers were unavailable.
assumptions: spec_check failure means any nonzero exit unless explicitly documented otherwise.
